abstract: Eukaryotic transcription machinery faces the dual challenge of having to dismantle the nucleosome barrier for efficient elongation and faithfully restore the chromatin landscape in its wake to prevent aberrant transcription. The sequence of molecular events from nucleosome unwrapping to reassembly has yet to be delineated. Here, we use a single-molecule platform to visualize the dynamics of chromatin transcription by mammalian elongation complex (EC) in real time. When supplemented with a set of elongation factors and histone chaperones, the EC can efficiently traverse the nucleosome it encounters and, surprisingly, carry the dislodged histones while continuing translocation on DNA, a phenomenon we termed histone 'hitchhiking'. The formation of this hitchhiking complex is facilitated by the elongation factor SPT6 and IWS1 through distinct mechanisms. On the other hand, the histone chaperones FACT and NAP1L1 promote the transition from histone hitchhiking to nucleosome reassembly. We further showed that the next nucleosome presents a strong barrier against the hitchhiking complex, thus limiting long-range chromatin disruption. Overall, our results revealed that histone hitchhiking by EC is a prevalent intermediate during chromatin transcription, and the timing and location of its resolution are tuned by multiple factors. This mechanism may provide the robustness and flexibility needed to maintain the local organization of transcriptionally active chromatin.
